description:
Plan: ../recursive-denotations-proposal.html. PR3 (fz-kdt.48), lands BEFORE fz-kdt.48.5.

Measured 2026-09-16 on fz-kdt.48/one-ty-per-denotation (2cb74c6bf and the .48.5 patch), instrumented seating + observe on both trees: at the Enum.drop_positive/take_positive call sites the decision tree asks the take arm's Region::Type question {:cont | :halt, C} (node n3) on a path that already holds the STRONGER proof Holds {:cont, C} (node n6 matched), so n3 is guaranteed to match and separates nothing: 7 of its 8 fires on 00183_enum_take_list_range are redundant, 2 of 3 on 00418_enum_count_range. Because of that redundant question, the ORDER of two already-Separated arms changes the number of matched questions per round, and the construction-coverage census (SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS in drive_test compiler2_no_value_reaches_a_construction_member_that_never_named_it) measures walk length: the parent seats the take arm first via lex_elements_then_longer's DNF clause-count tie-break (order.rs, b.len().cmp(&a.len())) reached from canonically_order_separated_neighbours (callsite_dispatch.rs ~376/397); .48.5's tuple fusion removes that clause-count axis, the arms transpose (stdout byte-identical, routing identical, no question added or removed), and the census moves 82->79 x3, 382->353 x2, 12->14 x2.

Build: when the plan constructs a Region::Type (whole-value) question at a node whose path already carries a Holds proof of a SUBTYPE of that question, the question is discharged (the node collapses to its match edge). Decide from the plan's own typed facts (Types::is_subtype on the question types), never from clause count or rendering. Then the order of Separated arms is a determinism choice only and census-neutral: prove it by flipping the tie-break in a test/probe and showing every census row unchanged. Expected: 00183 79 -> ~72 (inferred), every row at or below today's; no golden rises; pins lowered in the same motion. Tests: a decision-tree unit test with the two-arm witness (weaker question discharged, arm order irrelevant to matched-question count), plus the census pins. Doc: the dispatch planner doc gains the discharge rule; order.rs / callsite_dispatch.rs docs state that separated-arm order is determinism only. Unblocks fz-kdt.48.5, whose held patch then only lowers the census.

comments.text: Built and measured 2026-09-16 on d25552951 (patch 48-10.patch held, not committed). Rule lives in dispatch_matrix (Proven carried down during construction; Proof::settles; resolved_target; relation = Types::covers = RuntimeTypePredicate::contained_in on the two TESTS, memoized as ComparisonKey::TestCovers, NOT is_subtype: the type->test projection is not monotone, e.g. {any,any} & not({:x,:x}) projects to a test admitting no tuple). Gate green (lib 2210/0, matrix 825/0). Findings: (1) the rebase onto main already moved SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS rows: 82->64, 12->9, 382->265 at d25552951; (2) on the settled seat the discharge moves NO row (the question it removes is a refuted one, never matched); plan node counts unchanged, only 4/2/4/2/2/0 miss edges retarget; (3) the ticket's neutrality claim is REFUTED: with the tie-break flipped, rows are 61/11/236 without the rule and 54/9/225 with it, still not equal to the settled 64/9/265 either way; cause = when the covering arm is seated first a value answers the covering question, fails the closure, then answers the covered question, and nothing on that path settles the covering question; (4) the patch is net +8 concepts (Proven, RegionCovers, Proof::settles, resolved_target, Types::covers, TestCovers, PatternResolver::covers, impl PatternResolver for Types) minus 2 no-op resolvers. The cure that makes arm order free by construction is asking the SEPARATING position first within an arm (dispatch_row precondition order): 2 questions in either seat. Also proposed, not filed: a dispatch graph holding only root-reachable nodes (61 unreachable fail nodes on json_roundtrip at baseline); one authority for test coverage (runtime_questions/seating re-project what Types::covers memoizes).

title: Discharge a dispatch question already proven by a stronger one on the path
